digest.component_or_area: close STATUS event schema and completion-expectation recording
propositions: A close whose completion-signature append failed is indistinguishable from a gate-off close when read later, because gate state at close time is read from config and discarded, collapsing multiple closure reasons into a single gate-off state.

The completion_expectation enum (8 values: required, disposition, gate_off, gate_unreadable, force_bypassed, local_source, not_certifiable, not_applicable) must be persisted as a present-only field on the *->closed STATUS event in the same locked write as the close, so a later reader can combine it with durable attestation to distinguish signed, signature-lost, and gate-off closes.

The completion_expectation is computed by _completion_precheck as the second element of a returned pair (not from verified_result, which is None for --force closes despite a signature being expected), with gate state resolving first so --force under disabled/unreadable config records gate_off/gate_unreadable rather than force_bypassed.

The not_applicable value is set explicitly on the idea->closed transition path in close_ticket, which is the only place that knows the gate never applied, since idea->closed bypasses _completion_precheck entirely.
Historical close events lacking completion_expectation reduce to state with the key absent (unknown, never guessed), ensuring backward compatibility without migration.

A reader holding no lock and reading only reduced state can separate closed-and-signed (required + attestation), closed-with-signature-lost (required, no attestation), closed-with-gate-off (gate_off), and other closure reasons by consulting the completion_expectation field.
